audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven rows contradicted their own explanation. Packet levelChart reads Warwick, Skill, Warwick, Warwick, Warwick, Fiora, Fiora and every why tracks it; the stored sides read Fiora, Fiora, Fiora, Skill, Fiora, Skill, Fiora — so whys[0] 'Level 1 is yours' sat under a row labelled Fiora at 2/10.
audit.why: The prose and the packet agree, and a 56.7% Warwick win rate over 619 games with a late-game fall-off matches the packet shape, not the stored one. The mirror then corrects one row: level 6 reads Skill.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-5 set to the packet chart with the mirror's level-6 correction applied, in both layers as one atomic group; ratings re-keyed; whys[4] rewritten to the even read.

audit.whatIsWrong: Riposte is called matchup-defining on every screen and its cooldown is never given, nor is either ultimate's.
audit.why: Riposte is 24s at rank 1 and drops only to 16s at rank 5 — that gap is the entire all-in window. Both ultimates are 110s at rank 1, which is why level 6 is even rather than yours.
audit.corrected: 24s Riposte written into spikes[1], mid and phases[4].why; the matching 110s ultimates into whys[4].

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] says 'Infinite Duress is un-Riposteable damage-over-time you can bait her W with'. That is wrong twice over and it directly contradicts dontsFull[0] on the same page ('R into her Riposte'). Riposte parries ALL incoming damage and disables, and it stuns the attacker specifically when it blocks an immobilising effect — which a 1.5s suppression is. Leaping into it is the single worst play in the lane and the entry recommends it.
audit.why: Riot's W text: 'Fiora parries all incoming damage and disables for a short time... or stuns them if Fiora blocked an immobilizing effect with this ability.' Infinite Duress applies exactly such an effect.
audit.corrected: spikes[1], mid, spikes[3] and phases[4].why rewritten to state that Riposte parries the leap and stuns you for it, so the W must be spent before you commit.

edits.before: Level 6 is yours: baited Riposte plus Infinite Duress beats her Grand Challenge.
edits.after: Level 6 is even: both ultimates are 110s, and Riposte decides who lands first.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is un-Riposteable damage-over-time you can bait her W with — ult after she wastes Riposte and your suppress beats her Grand Challenge before it heals her up.
edits.after: Riposte parries all incoming damage and stuns whoever it blocks an immobilising effect from — so leaping into it hands her the fight. Bait the 24s W out, then commit.

edits.before: Full-build Fiora shreds you — vital true damage plus Grand Challenge (R) heal out-DPS and out-sustain your Q, and a clean Riposte negates your all-in entirely.
edits.after: Full-build Fiora shreds you — Grand Challenge's true damage and its area heal out-pace your Q, and one Riposte turns your leap into a stun on yourself.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 stay yours: Blood Hunt glues you to her so she can't kite vitals, and your Q sustain out-trades her early duel damage. At 6, force out her Riposte first, then Infinite Duress — the suppress and DoT beat her Grand Challenge if W is on cooldown.
edits.after: Levels 3-5 stay yours: Blood Hunt glues you to her once she drops under 50%, and Jaws of the Beast out-trades her early duel damage. At 6 it evens out — Riposte is 24s at rank 1, and if it blocks your suppression she stuns you, so bait it before you leap.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Fiora's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Riposte parries all damage and stuns you if it blocks your suppression — bait the 24s W before you ever spend a 110s Infinite Duress.

edits.before: Infinite Duress is a point-and-click fight starter that locks his carry tool — build your teamfight around that. Fiora carry threat: 10/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is a directional leap, and Riposte both parries it and stuns you for it — build the fight around baiting W. Fiora carry threat: 10/10 — anti-heal stays core, shift to picks if she gets ahead.

edits.before: Q-bite Fiora as he steps up (hold Q to follow his dash), weave autos, and let the passive out-heal his return damage.
edits.after: Q-bite Fiora as she steps up (hold Q to follow her Lunge), weave autos, and let Eternal Hunger heal you under 50%.

notes: The worst error in the whole slice is here: spikes[1] told the reader Infinite Duress is 'un-Riposteable' and to use it to bait her W. Riposte parries all incoming damage AND stuns the attacker when it blocks an immobilising effect, which a suppression is — so the page was recommending the exact play that loses the duel, while dontsFull[0] on the same page said the opposite. Chart rebuilt from the packet with the mirror's level-6 correction. NOTE: the mirror also recorded win[6] = 'Warwick' on Fiora's page, which inverts to Fiora on ours — that matches what is already stored, so row 6 was left untouched; if the mirror meant it the other way the two pages will need reconciling. Also left alone: whether Riposte's stun can break an already-applied suppression, which is not answerable from the kit files.
